core_obligations: Build the map from invertible sheaves to torsors: for an invertible O-module L consider the presheaf L^* of sections s such that multiplication by s is an isomorphism, show it satisfies the sheaf condition, that it carries a simply transitive action of O^* by multiplication, and that it has sections locally; hence L^* is an O^*-torsor and one gets a map from invertible sheaves up to isomorphism to O^*-torsors up to isomorphism, which the author does not check to be a group homomorphism (proof lines 531-559).
Reduce to bijectivity on torsors: by the torsor-H^1 identification the right-hand side is H^1(C, O^*), so it remains to show the constructed map is injective and surjective (proof lines 560-564).

Injectivity and surjectivity: if L^* is trivial then, by the triviality criterion, L^* has a global section, which forces L to be free, giving injectivity; conversely, starting from an O^*-torsor F one forms the presheaf L_1 = (F x O)/O^* with the described O-module structure, sheafifies to L, and by construction the associated torsor L^* is F, giving surjectivity; the author leaves the verification of this last point to the reader (proof lines 566-589).
proof_roadmap: Associate to an invertible module its sheaf of nondegenerate sections and observe that it is an O^*-torsor (proof lines 531-558).
Use the standard identification of torsors with H^1 of the units to reduce the statement to injectivity and surjectivity of that association (proof lines 560-564).
Prove injectivity via the trivial-torsor criterion, and surjectivity by an explicit construction with the quotient presheaf (F x O)/O^* and its sheafification (proof lines 566-589).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies H^1(C, O^*) with the Picard group of a locally ringed site (statement lines 522-527). The proof has to build the dictionary in both directions: the forward map sends an invertible module to its sheaf of nondegenerate sections, for which one must verify the sheaf condition, the simply transitive O^*-action and local existence of sections, and the backward map starts from an O^*-torsor and manufactures an invertible module from the quotient presheaf (F x O)/O^* with the action (s, g) -> (fs, f^{-1}g) (proof lines 531-585). Only after both maps exist does the reduction through torsor cohomology make sense. The author leaves two verifications to the reader, including that the twice-constructed composites are the identity; both sentences are reproduced as written. The claim is H2: two explicit constructions with the locally ringed hypothesis used exactly in the backward direction.
